stem: A medical-surgical unit identifies an increase in client falls and begins a performance-improvement project. Which action by the RN best reflects the nurse's role in this process?

options.A: Review unit data and relevant evidence with the quality team, participate in an approved improvement plan, and evaluate its effect on client outcomes
options.B: Change the unit fall-prevention policy independently after reviewing a single fall event and evaluate the change only if another fall occurs
options.C: Document each fall in the individual medical record but avoid using aggregate unit data because quality improvement is limited to management staff
options.D: Wait for an accrediting organization to prescribe the intervention before reporting the unit trend or participating in corrective action

rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement) within Management of Care. RN activities include participating in performance-improvement projects, reporting identified client-care issues, using research and other references for improvement actions, and evaluating the impact of improvement measures on client care and resource use. Option A incorporates these functions. The other options either bypass organizational processes and adequate evidence, exclude the RN from quality improvement, or delay reporting and action while waiting for an external body.
educational_objective: Participate in quality improvement by using client-care data and evidence, collaborating in approved improvement actions, and evaluating whether the intervention improves client outcomes.

correction_summary: Removed the original DNP-versus-PhD degree-comparison trivia because it lacks a strong NCLEX client-care construct. Rebuilt the item around NCSBN 2026 Performance Improvement/Quality Improvement with a realistic unit safety problem, evidence use, collaborative action, and outcome evaluation.
audit_findings: A directly integrates the NCSBN-listed RN quality-improvement activities. B relies on a single event and unilateral policy change; C incorrectly excludes staff RNs from QI and aggregate data use; D delays required reporting and participation pending external direction. The scenario is clinically relevant, contains no unsupported thresholds, and has no second defensible answer. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
